stories.title: Imran being forced into Benazir, Nawaz-style deal, claims Achakzai
summary: Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had reached its peak. “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” he told reporters, adding that a cabinet member had himself acknowledged that the system had collapsed.

TTAP challenges governor’s rule Meanwhile on Friday, TTAP leaders challenged the proclamation of emergency and imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before the PHC, seeking to have the measures declared unconstitutional and illegal.
They challenged the purported transfer of the KP Assembly’s legislative powers to parliament and the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet.

stories.title: Islamabad ATC rejects police request for physical remand of ex-GB CM Khalid Khurshid
summary: A case was registered against Khurshid, the president of the PTI’s GB chapter, at Aabpara Police Station in connection with the party’s November 26 protest in 2024.

PTI workers discharged In a separate development, the court also discharged PTI workers arrested in connection with two cases linked to the party’s recent long march after rejecting a request by the investigating officer for an adjournment to conduct their identification parade.

During proceedings concerning the PTI workers arrested in two cases registered at Shalimar and Secretariat police stations, the investigating officer requested an adjournment to conduct an identification parade.

stories.title: Karachi judicial magistrate extends physical remand of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan by 2 days
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Saturday extended the physical remand of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan by two days, directing the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to produce him on Oct 19 (Monday).

The magistrate also dismissed a plea filed by Hassan’s counsel under Section 63 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), which sought his discharge from the case. “He/accused did not claim any maltreatment at the hands of NCCIA.
The NCCIA, under Section 167 of the CrPC, presented the first remand report before the magistrate, seeking Hassan’s further physical remand for 10 days.

stories.title: Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP, PM reiterates
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday reiterated that the Centre was “compelled” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to the provincial government’s lack of cooperation in countering terrorism.
The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
The premier added that he assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in fighting against terrorism together to face the security challenges in the province.

stories.title: Shaheen Afridi wants unity to be Pakistan's identity under his leadership
summary: Unlike in 2024, when he was removed as Pakistan’s T20 captain after just one series in charge, the country’s cricket board appears to have committed to giving Shaheen a longer run as leader.
Appointed to the ODI role 12 months ago, he is expected to lead Pakistan through to next year’s World Cup in South Africa.
When Pakistan take on Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ODI tri-series on Sunday, Shaheen will have Babar Azam among his charges.

stories.title: Islamabad ATC summons Islamabad police chief in security breach case against Imaan and Hadi
summary: During the proceedings, the court expressed displeasure over the continued absence of the investigating officer and raised questions about the whereabouts of the case record.
Advocate Zafar Khokhar also questioned under which law an investigating officer could take the case record away and leave court proceedings stalled.
On Oct 15, the court directed lawyers and witnesses in the case to appear at Adiala jail for the next hearing after police cited difficulties in transporting the couple to court.

stories.title: Minister rebukes JUI-F chief for seeking ‘share’ in KP governance after imposition of governor’s rule, emergency
summary: State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on Saturday rebuked Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman for reportedly seeking his “share” in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province.
He was seemingly referring to Fazl who has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI.

stories.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine.

The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.

Zelensky asked the bloc — Ukraine’s biggest international backer — to provide more Patriot missiles to shoot down Russian missiles and come up with an extra 70 billion euros ($79 billion) in support next year to help Kyiv keep fighting.

stories.title: Egypt's President Sisi pledges to leave office when term ends in 2030
summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that he would not seek to remain in office when his current term expires in 2030, describing the matter as “completely settled”.

Speaking to graduates and state officials in the sprawling new city east of Cairo, Sisi said the Egyptian constitution “would not be touched”. “The period leading up to 2030 will be the end of my term as president of the state, if I am still alive.
Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and included transitional provisions that allowed Sisi to run for an additional term.

stories.title: Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery
summary: Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said on Saturday, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”.
The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”. “He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican.
Up in air News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.

stories.title: Armed men abduct 20 under-training police personnel in Mastung: officials
summary: QUETTA: Unidentified armed men kidnapped 20 police recruits undergoing training at the Kalat Police Training Centre while they were travelling in a passenger van along the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Mastung district, officials said.
He said a group of armed men riding motorcycles and carrying automatic weapons intercepted the van and took the recruits away along with the vehicle to an undisclosed location.
Police officials in Mastung also confirmed the abduction, saying the recruits belonged to the Levies Force, which has since been merged with the police.

stories.title: After the emergency
summary: The federal government simultaneously invoked Article 234 apparently to render the provincial assembly non-functional during the emergency and to vest all legislative powers in parliament.

Both articles concern the proclamation of an emergency, and both give the federal government the option to either exercise executive powers directly in the province or designate the provincial governor to do so on its behalf.
Given the clear majority of the ruling coalition and the PPP, continuing the proclamation of emergency under this article for six months doesn’t seem to pose a challenge for the federal government.

stories.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder arrested after detention, media reports say
summary: Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of ​a house in central ​Delhi, with police hauling ⁠him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument.
Dipke had called Friday’s protest in support of two CJP leaders detained ​and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at ​a protest ⁠site in violation of a ban.
Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

stories.title: North Korea says tested AI-assisted torpedo system
summary: Earlier this month, North Korea announced the AI-assisted launch of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

Days after North Korea announced it had tested its AI-assisted intermediate-range hypersonic missile, Seoul test-fired its own weapon – a hypersonic glide vehicle it called a “key strategic asset capable of changing the course of the battlefield”.
North Korea this week cast doubt on Seoul’s test, saying it may have “failed to achieve hypersonic flight”, a claim South Korea rejected a day later.

stories.title: Pakistan seek solid start against Sri Lanka
summary: Pakistan will look to make a strong start when they face Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday, with the match scheduled to begin at 1pm.

He added that Babar, who captained Pakistan for five years, remained an important figure for younger players to learn from. “Babar is the backbone of the team,” Shaheen said, noting that the batsman had also been working on his form in first-class cricket.
Pakistan have won several recent series but have been unable to complete a clean sweep, Shaheen said, adding that the team continued to work towards greater consistency.

stories.title: 5.9-magnitude earthquake jolts Balochistan's Khuzdar
summary: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake jolted Balochistan’s Khuzdar district on Saturday, according to the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD).
The PMD said the earthquake’s epicentre was located 48 kilometres northwest of Khuzdar, at latitude 28.02 degrees north and longitude 66.20 degrees east.
According to the seismological centre, the earthquake was recorded at a depth of 15 kilometres, with its epicentre located 122km northeast of Zhob.

stories.title: SSGC warns parts of Karachi may face gas supply disruption tomorrow
summary: Parts of Karachi may experience low gas pressure on Sunday following scheduled maintenance work on a 24-inch Qatar mainline in the Sher Shah area, Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) said in a statement.
SSGC said the work had been scheduled during the hours when domestic gas supply was normally suspended.
The SITE Industrial Area may also be affected if the maintenance work takes longer than scheduled.

stories.title: Anthropic proposes law regulating AI to US lawmakers
summary: Anthropic, the creator of the AI assistant Claude, confirmed on Friday it is circulating a draft bill among US lawmakers aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to address the lack of federal legislation on the risks posed by the new technology.
Anthropic, which was banned from the Pentagon by the Trump administration in February, was forced by Washington in June to suspend its most advanced models for nearly three weeks.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the industry last month to slow down development, fearing that a group of AI agents could take control of “the entire internet” within six to 12 months.

stories.title: Over 340 children killed in Gaza since ceasefire, says Unicef
summary: The Unicef noted that five boys and two girls had been reported killed in Gaza over the preceding two weeks, while at least 33 children were seriously injured in air strikes, drone strikes and gunfire across the territory.

Children needed to return to school, spend time with friends and family, have dignified shelter, play safely and receive healthcare, the agency said. “Gaza’s children have suffered far too much, for far too long,” it added.
Despite the continuing hardship, Unicef has helped more than 560,000 children return to learning since the ceasefire, including through more than 200 learning centres it supports.

stories.title: Pakistan whip China in Johor Cup
summary: Pakistan’s junior hockey team opened their Sultan of Johor Cup 2026 campaign with an emphatic 8-3 victory over China, producing an attacking display to start the tournament on a winning note.
Rana Waleed scored in the 37th minute, followed by Hamza Fayyaz’s strike two minutes later, as Pakistan strengthened their grip on the match.
Mustafa Ghulam added another goal in the 43rd minute, while Usman Muhammad struck a minute later to extend Pakistan’s advantage.

stories.title: Pakistan face SAFF preparation crisis
summary: Pakistan’s preparations for the SAFF Championship have come under scrutiny, with the national team set to begin its training camp on October 26, just nine days before the tournament kicks off in Dhaka, raising concerns over the players’ fitness and readiness.
Pakistan’s head coach Nolberto Solano confirmed to this correspondent that the training camp would begin on October 26, just nine days before the team’s opening match against India on November 5.
Unlike India and Bangladesh, where domestic leagues provide players with regular competition and help maintain their fitness, Pakistan currently has no active domestic league.

stories.title: K-P is rich in minerals; we will 'extract and sell them', says Kundi
summary: Kundi assailed Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman over his stance against the governor’s rule in the province, saying the government had been formed without his support and would continue to function successfully.

Kundi questions Fazl’s stance on K-P governor’s rule Taking a jibe at the JUI-F chief, Governor Kundi said, “Maulana himself used to say — I have heard him say — that no government could be formed without him, and that if one were formed, it would not be able to function.

Softening his approach towards the JUI-F chief, Kundi invited Fazl to work with the government to promote peace, development and prosperity in the province, saying political differences should not obstruct efforts to improve the lives of the people.

stories.title: Trump waives key Russia-related sanctions, tariffs before they take effect under new law
summary: US President Donald ​Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs days before they were to take effect under a law he ‌signed last month, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas.

Read: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies "I have submitted to Congress a certification that the issuance ‌of ⁠such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order.

Putin's investment envoy, ​Kirill Dmitriev, called Trump's waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X that the legislation could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt.

stories.title: Armed men abduct 20 trainee police personnel travelling from Kalat to Nushki: officials
summary: Twenty trainee police personnel on Saturday were abducted by unidentified armed men while travelling between Kalat and Mastung in Balochistan, provincial government and police officials told The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.

They further added that the armed men abducted the personnel from within the limits of Kalat district and took them to the Gargina-Kardgap area of Mastung district before moving them to an undisclosed location.
According to Turbat police, the labourers were abducted by unidentified armed men after their vehicle was intercepted near Kalatak in Turbat.

stories.title: Fazl seeks joint in-camera session as ministers reject 'spoils of war' charge
summary: Speaking to reporters in Lahore, Fazl urged the government to convene an in-camera session of parliament to brief lawmakers on the security situation and its counterterrorism strategy, questioning why the nation was not being taken into confidence.
They have never issued a press release for any other political party,” Talal said, referring to a statement by the banned outfit opposing the imposition of governor's rule in K-P.
The federal government defended the decision by citing security concerns and a lack of cooperation from the provincial government.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court directs LEAs not to arrest, harass former AG
summary: In a short order, the bench said the petitioner should not be arrested or harassed until the next hearing into the case on Oct 20.
Lawyer Yasir Khattak appeared for the petitioner, while advocate general Sanaullah represented the government.

The petition said the incident and the conduct of the officials concerned had given rise to a genuine and reasonable apprehension that the petitioner would be unlawfully arrested or detained without due process of law.

stories.title: Five schools sealed in Khyber
summary: KHYBER: Authorities sealed five private schools on Friday after their buildings were found to be in extremely poor condition.
Officials in Landi Kotal, Bara and Jamrud said that assistant commissioners in the three tehsils paid visits to a number of private schools to inspect the buildings’ condition.
Officials said that five schools, which were sealed in Landi Kotal, Bara and Jamrud, were found to be in very poor condition, posing a threat to the lives of both students and teachers.

stories.title: Robbers strike three times in 40 minutes in Islamabad's D-12
summary: The robbers held him up and looted Rs7,000 in cash and a mobile phone worth Rs60,000.
At around 1:10am, the robbers intercepted another delivery rider, Asim Mehmood, who was returning after delivering an order in D-12/1.
They looted Rs8,000 in cash and a mobile phone worth Rs68,000 before disappearing into the wooded area again.

stories.title: Rawalpindi's Chahan Dam water supply project to be completed by 2027: minister
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Chahan Dam water supply project is expected to be completed by December 2027, helping address water shortages in several parts of the garrison city and benefiting more than 250,000 people.

Rs35bn project to provide clean drinking water to over 250,000 people in Rawalpindi Wasa officials briefed the minister that the project was being executed with financial assistance from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Punjab government.

During the visit, Mr Ranjha briefed the minister on completed and ongoing horticultural projects, including initiatives to improve public recreational facilities, parks, squares, roundabouts and other public spaces across Rawalpindi.

stories.title: Rs615m recovered from illegal visa agents in Islamabad in four months: FIA
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Islamabad Zone arrested 190 illegal visa agents and recovered Rs615.55m during the last four months in crackdowns on human smuggling and fraud.
AHTC Rawalpindi arrested 70 agents, recovered Rs204.5m and registered 668 cases.
The FIA said it was continuing steps to protect citizens from fraud in the name of overseas employment and travel, take legal action against illegal visa agents and prevent human smuggling.

stories.title: Four suspects held for ‘kidnapping’ woman in Taxila
summary: TAXILA: Police arrested four suspects, including the alleged ringleader, in Jand town of Attock for abducting a woman at gunpoint and seriously injuring her brother after shooting him over resistance after a marriage proposal was reportedly rejected, police said on Friday.
Police said the incident stemmed from the family’s refusal to accept a marriage proposal.
The abducted woman was recovered safely, police said.

stories.title: Sindh govt plan to raise retirement age for university professors by five years
summary: The information was shared by Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah during a meeting with the vice chancellors of 32 public sector universities here on Friday.
The chief secretary said the challenges facing universities required coordinated efforts by the provincial government, university administrations and relevant federal institutions.

He said the government would continue consultations with vice chancellors to address issues affecting the performance, financial sustainability and academic development of public sector universities in Sindh.

stories.title: Karachi court extends journalist Iqrarul Hassan's physical remand by two days
summary: A Karachi court on Saturday extended journalist Iqrarul Hassan's physical remand by two days in a case of harming the state and national integrity by disseminating anti-state content.
Last week, the NCCIA produced Hassan before the judicial magistrate, who handed the journalist over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand.

On Thursday, the District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters.

stories.title: NHA cuts trees planted by Karachi's Baldia Town to widen Hub River Road
summary: KARACHI: While the city is already struggling with the issue of its low and rapidly declining tree cover, hundreds of semi-mature neem trees along the eight-kilometre-long stretch of Hub River Road wait for their turn to be chopped down, one by one.
To gain data on the relocated trees, Dawn tried to obtain information on the tree plantation drive and the number of trees relocated or lost under the current development phase from TMC Baldia.

Despite the inadequate information on the number of saplings planted across the Hub River Road stretch, one can witness both the emergence and vanishing of these saplings if one is a regular traveller commuting the said road like the writer.

stories.title: Bangladesh resort fire kills at least 10, injures 9 others
summary: At least 10 people, believed to be tourists, were killed, and nine others were injured in a fire at a resort on the Cox’s Bazar coast, a tourist hub in southeastern Bangladesh, on Saturday morning, the country's fire service confirmed.

The fire broke out at a wooden resort and restaurant at Inani Sea Beach in Cox's Bazar, the fire service said in a statement, adding that the blaze was completely extinguished after two firefighting units responded alongside local authorities and police.
Read: 'Gul Plaza management involved in fire tragedy' At least nine people were injured when the fire broke out early in the morning while they were asleep, Jamuna TV reported.

stories.title: LHC extends stay against deportation of Afghan students
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday extended a stay against expulsion and deportation of Afghan medical students and granted the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) more time to submit its reply.

A counsel for the PMDC told the court that the prime minister office had issued a direction to the relevant authorities to allow the Afghan students to continue their studies subject to valid visa and immigration requirements.
The court had on Sept 11 suspended the operation of the PMDC directives ordering Afghan medical students to return to the neighbouring country.

stories.title: Attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure pose risks to Pakistan's economic outlook: FinMin Aurangzeb
summary: In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Aurangzeb said Pakistan had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike.

The finance minister also met Jihad Azour, director of the IMF Middle East and Central Asia Department, to discuss Pakistan’s economic performance and reforms, the Ministry of Finance said on Saturday.
Aurangzeb reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sustaining primary surpluses, reducing public debt and advancing growth-friendly tax reforms while protecting social spending.

stories.title: Plea against 10-day Basant festival rejected in LHC
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday dismissed a petition challenging the Punjab government’s plan to hold the Basant festival for 10 days in 2027 after the petitioner failed to satisfy the court about its maintainability.
At the outset of the hearing, the judge asked the petitioner’s counsel how the proposed Basant festival could be challenged without a formal government notification.
The judge observed that the petition could not be based on unverified information and directed the counsel to obtain the official notification before challenging the government’s decision.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly body summons Gymkhana Club management over land lease controversy
summary: According to notices issued by Assembly Secretary General Chaudhry Amer Habib, the special committee convened by MPA Sami Ullah Khan is `intensifying’its probe into long-standing controversies surrounding the club’s occupation of government land.
The club also holds six acres of Bagh-e-Jinnah for a cricket ground, at Rs900 a year, on a lease running until 2069.
Resolution No 288 moved by Amjad Ali Javed and Rao Kashif Rahim Khan asks the government to turn 100 acres into a public park and urban forest, leaving 17 acres to the club.

stories.title: Ambassador Sheikh urges Pakistani-Americans to drive 'mutually rewarding' economic engagement
summary: It added that community representatives expressed their gratitude towards Sheikh for his participation, appreciating the embassy’s efforts to strengthen Pakistan-US relations.
The representatives also thanked the consulate general of Pakistan in Los Angeles for facilitating consular services for the Pakistani-American community in the area.
